completion.notes: Expresses regret or unintended completion. Often used with negative outcomes.

examples.japanese: 傘を忘れてしまいました
examples.english: I forgot my umbrella.

examples.japanese: スマホを落としちゃった
examples.english: I dropped my smartphone.

forms.verb: て-form + しまう / しまいました

completion.notes: Do something in advance or leave something in place. Shows foresight or convenience.

examples.japanese: クラスの前にカバンをまとめておきます
examples.english: I'll gather the bags before class.

examples.japanese: ビールを冷蔵庫に入れておきます
examples.english: I'll put the beer in the refrigerator.

examples.japanese: そのままにしておきます
examples.english: I will leave it as it is.

forms.verb: て-form + おく / おきます

completion.notes: Indicates an action just completed. Use after the ta-form of verbs.

examples.japanese: 日本に来たばかりです
examples.english: I just came to Japan

examples.japanese: アルバイトを始めたばかりなので、まだ仕事に慣れません
examples.english: Since I've just started my part-time job, I'm not used to the work yet.

examples.japanese: 仕事を辞めたばかりなのに、もう新しい仕事を見つけた
examples.english: Even though I just quit my job, I already found a new one

completion.notes: Do something exactly as instructed or expected. Attach after nouns or verbs.

examples.japanese: 先生の指示の通りに避難してください
examples.english: Please evacuate as directed by the teacher.

examples.japanese: 私の思った通り、事がうまく続いている
examples.english: Just as I expected, things are going well

examples.japanese: 期待どおり、Aチームが優秀した
examples.english: As expected, Team A excelled.

completion.notes: Expresses an incomplete action. Cannot be used with stative verbs.

examples.japanese: この作文は書きかけですから、全部書いて明日提出します。
examples.english: This essay is only half-finished, so I will complete it and submit it tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 風邪が治りかけていたのに、無理をしたので、またひどくなってしまった。
examples.english: I was on the verge of recovering from a cold, but because I overexerted myself, it got worse again.

forms.verb: masu-stem + かけだ / かけの + N / かける

completion.notes: Describes the sequence of events; attach to nouns.

examples.japanese: 卒業のあとで、会社で働き始めた
examples.english: After graduation, I started working at a company

completion.notes: Attach after past-tense verbs (ta-form). Shows sequence of actions.

examples.japanese: クラスが終わったあとで、買い物をしよう
examples.english: Let's go shopping after class ends.

examples.japanese: 家に帰ったあとで、シャワーを浴びました
examples.english: After I returned home, I took a shower.

completion.notes: Indicates an action completed before an important subsequent action.

examples.japanese: 書類の内容を読んだ上で、サインをお願いします
examples.english: Please sign this after reading the content of the document.

completion.notes: Indicates immediate action following completion of something within speaker's control.

examples.japanese: 準備が出来次第、発表を始めましょう
examples.english: As soon as we're ready, let's start the presentation

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わり次第、すぐそちらに向かいます
examples.english: As soon as I finish my work, I'll head straight to your location

completion.notes: に marks time; を marks another person or place causing action.

examples.japanese: 家を出ようとしたところに、雨が降ってきた
examples.english: Just as I was about to leave the house, it started to rain

examples.japanese: 昨日、階段で転んだところを人に見られて、とても恥ずかしかった
examples.english: Yesterday, I tripped on the stairs and someone saw me, which was very embarrassing.

forms.verb: dictionary/ta-form + ところに / ところを

completion.notes: Expresses the state immediately after or upon completion of an action.

examples.japanese: 新しいパソコンを買ったところ、とても使いやすかった
examples.english: I just bought a new computer, and it's very easy to use.

completion.notes: Use with non-volitional past-tense verbs. Sudden or unexpected events.

examples.japanese: 国の母に電話をかけた。母の声を聞いたとたんに、涙が出てきた。
examples.english: I called my mother back in my home country. The moment I heard her voice, tears started to fall.

examples.japanese: テレビで紹介されて有名になったとたんに、お店のサービスが悪くなった。
examples.english: As soon as it was featured on TV and became famous, the service at the store worsened.

completion.notes: Occurs immediately after or during an action. Use with dictionary, ta, or nai forms.

examples.japanese: バスが止まるが止まらないかのうちに席を立つ人が多い。
examples.english: Many people stand up from their seats while the bus is still deciding whether to stop or not.

examples.japanese: 昨夜は疲れていたので、ベッドに横になったかならないかのうちに、眠ってしまった。
examples.english: I was tired last night, so I fell asleep almost as soon as I lay in bed.

forms.verb: dictionary/ta-form/nai-form + か + verb + かのうちに

completion.notes: Emphasizes first experience or realization. Use directly after verbs.

examples.japanese: 病気になって初めて、家族の大切さがわかった。
examples.english: It was only after I fell ill that I understood the importance of family.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしになって初めて、母親のありがたさがわかった。
examples.english: It was only when I started living alone that I truly appreciated my mother.

completion.notes: Indicates necessary condition for action. Use with dictionary verbs or nouns.

examples.japanese: 仕事を進める上で、みんなの協力が必要だ。
examples.english: In progressing with work, everyone's cooperation is necessary.

examples.japanese: 共同生活をする上で大切なのは、お互いにルールを守ることです。
examples.english: In communal living, it's important to respect each other's rules.

completion.notes: Used with negative outcomes after a series of events. Attach after ta-form verbs.

examples.japanese: ５時間も話し合いを続けたあげく、何も決まらなかった。
examples.english: After discussing for five hours, we didn't decide on anything.

examples.japanese: 彼は散々悩んだ挙げ句、会社を辞めることに決めた。
examples.english: After much distress, he decided to resign from the company.

completion.notes: Indicates a single event since a point in time; often negative.

examples.japanese: この本は子どものころ読んだきり、その後一度も読んでいません。
examples.english: I haven't read this book since I first read it as a child.

examples.japanese: 彼に最後に会ったのは、卒業式の時です。それきり、一度も会いません。
examples.english: The last time I saw him was at the graduation ceremony. I haven't seen him even once since then.

completion.notes: Indicates something must be completed before a specific time.

examples.japanese: 2026までに日本語のが話せなければなりません
examples.english: I must be able to speak Japanese by 2026.

examples.japanese: 今週末までにチケットを買わなければなりません
examples.english: I have to buy a ticket by this weekend.

completion.notes: Do something before a condition changes. Often with negative verbs.

examples.japanese: 忘れてしまわないうちに、メモします
examples.english: I'll make a note of it before I forget.

completion.notes: Indicates an action almost happened but was prevented.

examples.japanese: もう少しで１００点取れるところだったのに。９５点だった。
examples.english: I was so close to getting 100 points, but I got 95.

forms.verb: dictionary form + ところだった

completion.notes: Used before important or ceremonial events; highly formal.

examples.japanese: 遊園地の開業に先立って、オープニングイベントが行われます
examples.english: An opening event will be held before the amusement park opens.
